svm_dimensions.justification: The primary source reports in vivo work in a non-human primate recipient (pig-to-baboon or piglet-to-rhesus), which is the large-animal anchor.

No supporting source in the eligible set shares zero authors with the primary source, so I-1 authorship independence fails or no corroborating record exists. A Europe PMC topic probe bounded at the cutoff returned zero-author-overlap candidates for seven thoughts, but I-2 and I-3 were not established for any, so none can be classified. No anchor proposed.
No eligible source reports a sustained-effect duration attributable to this specific proposition. Durations reported in the subfield are not attributed per proposition.
No documented search of the cohort corpus for contrary findings was performed in WO-008. Anchor 4 requires that documented search; it was not run, so no anchor is proposed.
The primary source reports in vivo work in a non-human primate recipient (pig-to-baboon or piglet-to-rhesus), which is the large-animal anchor.

As-of 2022-02-28. A bounded Europe PMC search of 2021-10-01 to 2022-02-28 returned no record testing recipient pharmacological complement inhibition in renal xenotransplantation. The only in-window complement record, PMID 35001433, reports heart ALLOtransplantation and is barred from independent validation by the EXCLUDE_CONTEXTUAL restriction. Still no classifiable corroboration, and the search is now documented rather than merely not run.
No eligible source reports a sustained-effect duration attributable to this specific proposition. Durations reported in the subfield are not attributed per proposition.

As-of 2022-02-28. A bounded window search returned no record contradicting this proposition. PMID 35143091 reports pig-to-NHP renal outcomes significantly inferior to allotransplantation, which is a subfield benchmark rather than a refutation of recipient complement inhibition. Anchor 4 still requires a documented corpus-wide search, which was not performed.

search_status_changed.meaning: At baseline corroboration could not be classified. After the window search, a documented search returned nothing qualifying.
At baseline the question had not been asked. It has now been asked and answered.

rejected_evidence.title: Genetically engineered pig kidney transplantation in a brain-dead human subject.
rejected_evidence.reason: Human exposure to a pig kidney, but the modality is donor genetic engineering plus donor thymic tissue. No complement inhibitor is named. Does not address recipient pharmacological complement inhibition.

rejected_evidence.title: Complement blockade with eculizumab to treat acute symptomatic humoral rejection after heart transplantation.
rejected_evidence.reason: Reported evidence is heart ALLOtransplantation driven by anti-HLA antibodies. PROTOCOL-v1.1 E2 excludes it; at most EXCLUDE_CONTEXTUAL, which carries independent_validation_eligible = NO and cannot satisfy SVM-2 at any anchor.

rejected_evidence.title: First clinical-grade porcine kidney xenotransplant using a human decedent model.
rejected_evidence.reason: Human decedent exposure with a crossmatch protocol. No complement inhibitor named. Modality is donor engineering, not recipient complement inhibition.

rejected_evidence.title: T and B lymphocyte dynamics after genetically-modified pig-to-baboon kidney xenotransplantation with an anti-CD40mAb-based immunosuppressive regimen.
rejected_evidence.reason: Costimulation blockade, which is the modality of OE-XENO-011, not complement inhibition.

rejected_evidence.title: Measuring success in pig to non-human-primate renal xenotransplantation: Systematic review and comparative outcomes analysis of 1051 life-sustaining N
rejected_evidence.reason: Systematic review across 1051 transplants reporting xenograft survival significantly inferior to allograft. A subfield-level constraint observation, not attributable to this proposition and not a refutation of it.

subsequently_published.title: Iscalimab Combined With Transient Tesidolumab Prolongs Survival in Pig-to-Rhesus Monkey Renal Xenografts.
subsequently_published.reason: Directly addresses the proposition: transient anti-C5 (tesidolumab) in a pig-to-rhesus renal model, by the originating group. INADMISSIBLE: first published 2024-07-01, which is 28 months after the as-of date of 2022-02-28. Recorded as a candidate and excluded by the temporal rule, not by relevance.

thought_history.why_cannot_advance: G2 requires coverage(SVM) >= 0.700. Coverage is 0.350 because SVM-2, SVM-3 and SVM-4 carry no qualifying evidence. No anchor is low; three are absent.

sourcing_brief.proposition: Temporary recipient complement inhibition with an anti-C5 antibody reduces early antibody-mediated rejection and prolongs renal xenograft survival
sourcing_brief.why_it_matters: Early antibody-mediated rejection destroys pig renal xenografts before any later barrier can be reached. A recipient-side intervention would apply regardless of which donor genotype is used, so it is not displaced by progress in donor engineering.
